title: Preparing for the Academic Job Market
description: Graduate students will have the job market process demystified while preparing a dossier of requested materials. Students will first study the rhetorical features associated with the major documents required for these positions and then produce discipline-specific drafts (with feedback provided).
prerequisites_raw: Students have to be, at the earliest, one year away from applying to the job market.

title: Writing Studies: Histories, Theories, and Methods
description: This course provides an introduction to the history, theory, and research considerations of Writing Studies. It focuses on foundational historical movements in composition pedagogy, current trends in Writing Studies, and interdisciplinary approaches to the field, including selected research methodologies.

title: Pedagogies of University Writing: Theory and Practice
description: Explores theoretical foundations and practical approaches to teaching writing at the university and college level. Students will examine pedagogical theories, design writing prompts, and develop strategies for assessment and providing feedback. Assignments include writing teaching philosophies, crafting course materials, facilitating discussion, and reflective writing. By integrating theory and practice, students will gain a deeper understanding of the various facets involved in teaching writing in a postsecondary context.

Topics include theories of composition pedagogy, academic literacies, principles of instructional design and curriculum development, effective classroom practices, and assessment of student writing.
prerequisites_raw: Application submitted for Writing Program TA appointment.

title: Rome: The Game
description: This online course presented as an adventure game introduces students to the art and archaeology of Rome, with assignments that focus on writing and the research process. The course asks students to determine whether or not a collection of ancient objects from an American museum should remain in the US or be sent back to Italy. Throughout the course, students excavate artifacts at a digital dig site, visit museums, explore Roman monuments, and navigate the shadowy world of the tombaroli (tomb robbers) and mafia-run black market for antiquities.

title: Multimedia Writing Online
description: Focuses on new modes of writing and publishing enabled by computer technology. Projects involve analyzing, creating, reading about, and reflecting on multimedia writing. Students create works suitable for web or other digital formats.

title: Business and Administrative Writing
description: Analysis and practice in business genres that focus on writing strategy, concise style, and visual aspects of communication. Attention to typical documents such as letters, memos, e-mail, proposals, and collaborative reports. Courses also typically integrate oral presentations, job search documents, and the use of relevant technology.

title: Legal Writing
description: Practice in applying rules to facts, analyzing issues, and writing clearly, succinctly, and cogently in various forms of legal discourse such as case briefs, law essays, persuasive letters, short office memoranda, mediation and appellate briefs. Fundamentals of legal research are touched upon.

title: Writing Web Content Online
description: An online course in which students analyze the rhetorical strategies underlying creation of Web 2.0 content. Students create common content modalities that may include Websites, blogs, email newsletters, and social media as used in professional contexts.
prerequisites_raw: Writ 2 or Writ 2LK or Writ 2E or AP36 >=4 or AP 37 >=4 or WAIV AW >=1 or IB BL >=6 or IB E >=6; upper division standing
